outcome: hospital resource utilization (length of stay, total hospital charges)
type of anesthesia-related complications (spinal cord complications, adverse effects, systemic complications)
cohort: The study included 592,868 hospital deliveries in North Carolina between 2015 and 2020.
finding: Anesthesia-related complications during labor and delivery are relatively uncommon (2.9/1000 discharges) but are associated with distinct demographic, clinical, and hospital-level risk factors, including advanced maternal age, specific racial/ethnic groups, non-traditional insurance, higher comorbidity, and cesarean section delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean section deliveries were associated with a higher risk of anesthesia-related complications.
